verdict.rationale: The IRS publishes a sanctioned third-party designee role for EIN applications, which requires signed authorization from the responsible party. It also states that signed mobile-friendly forms (e.g., the 83(b) Form 15620) require the taxpayer's own Online Account, behind ID.me biometric verification, so those signatures stay personal. Separately, it documents the credentialed Authorized e-file Provider role. Missing for 10: a consolidated published statement of what third parties may and may not do (e.g., power-of-attorney or tax-information authorization forms and their scopes), named authorization forms beyond the EIN designee note, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: a third-party designee may apply, with signed authorization from the responsible party
Online Account (OLA) is required to complete mobile friendly forms that require signatures
You'll need an account with ID.me to sign in to access your tax information and use services on IRS.gov.
